subject: pe
title: Warm-Up: Why & How
welcome_lead: A good warm-up prepares body and brain — and cuts injury risk.
meta_desc: KS3 PE: pulse raise, mobilisation, dynamic stretches.
final_note: Five minutes of warm-up beats five weeks of injury.

walkthroughs.body_html: Start with light jogging, skipping or cycling for 3-5 minutes. Heart and muscles warm up; blood flow increases.
Move joints with shoulder rolls, arm swings, leg swings. Dynamic stretches like lunges prepare muscles for action.
Cold muscles tear more easily. Warming up reduces injury risk and improves performance.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between aerobic and muscular endurance?
options: Aerobic endurance is the cardiovascular system's ability to supply oxygen; muscular endurance is a muscle's ability to contract repeatedly without fatigue.
Aerobic is for legs, muscular for arms.
They are different names for the same component.

mcqs.q: What sport is best suited to type I (slow-twitch) fibres?
options: Strength is for the upper body, power for the lower.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between strength and power?
options: Strength is maximum force; power is force times speed of movement.
Aerobic is for legs, muscular for arms.
Strength is for the upper body, power for the lower.
